figures.finding: Iraq taxes all Iraq-source income on a scale of 3% to IQD 250,000, 5% to 500,000, 10% to 1,000,000 and 15% above.

value.regional: Kurdistan region applies its own instructions

figures.finding: The employer deducts income tax from salaries monthly (PAYE) and pays it within the first 15 days of the next month; the year is reconciled at year end.

sources.said: The employer is responsible for deducting the staff income tax from their salaries, and forwarding that amount to the General Commission of Taxes/Direct Deduction Division within a period not exceeding the first 15 days of the next month in which the assessment was incurred.

figures.finding: Social security is 5% from the employee and 12% from the employer (25% for employers classed as prime), on net salary after allowances, for local and expatriate staff.

sources.said: The employer's contribution is 12% and the employee's contribution is 5% from net salaries. The contribution of employers that are categorised as prime will be 25%.

figures.finding: In the Kurdistan region a non-resident's contract as an athlete or artist is taxed at 15% on a deemed profit of 30% of the contract; federally, payments to non-residents for interest and similar items bear 15%.

sources.said: The non-resident entity in Iraq will be subject to WHT at a rate of 15% from the deemed profit determined by the Ministry of Finance.
8. The contract of athletes and artists 30

figures.finding: Iraq has no general VAT; a 2015 sales tax applies to listed goods and services (10% on luxury hotel and restaurant services).

sources.said: A new sales tax law was issued in early 2015 whereby a sales tax of 300% will be imposed on alcohol and tobacco (cigarettes), 15% on travel tickets, 15% on cars, and 20% on mobile recharge cards and internet.

figures.finding: Income tax falls due at the end of the financial year in which the income arose, and the income tax return must be filed on or before 31 May each year; a late return costs 10% of the tax, at most IQD 500,000.

value.taxYear: financial year (assessment in the following year)

figures.applies: Taxpayers under Income Tax Law No. 113 of 1982 as amended (General Commission for Taxes guide).
